fixes.explanation: Forty years is how long Joash reigned, and that's in verse 1. But this verse measures his right-doing on a different clock: “…all the days of Jehoiada the priest.” That's the time the text names here. Two clocks, friend, and this verse is reading the Jehoiada one.

You got it, baker. Joash says, “Do it quickly.” and then the text says, “The Levites, however, did not make haste.” That one little word "however" turns the whole verse around. It's like a friend who says "two minutes!" and then sits back down on the couch.
Yes, baker! The chest is made at the king's command and “…placed outside, at the gate of the house of the LORD.” Not inside, but outside at the gate. A chest, a gate and a king's command, friend.
The altar isn't the spot the text gives for this chest. It says the chest was “…placed outside, at the gate of the house of the LORD.” Outside, friend, at the gate.

A treasury sounds like a natural spot for money, I'll give you that. But the text says the chest was “…placed outside, at the gate of the house of the LORD.” Outside at the gate is a long way from the back of the junk drawer I got stuck in for years, friend, and I would know.

Hesitating isn't in this verse, friend. The text says all the officers and all the people “…rejoiced and brought their contributions, and they dropped them in the chest until it was full.” Officers too, not just the regular folks.

That's right, baker. The text says the royal scribe and the high priest's officer would come and empty the chest and carry it back to its place, and “They did this daily…” Every single day. That's a very regular schedule.

That's a nice crew, but the text doesn't list them here. It says the money hired “…stonecutters and carpenters…” and also “…workers in iron and bronze…” Those are the workers named for the repair, friend.

That's right, baker. The text says, “They restored the house of God according to its specifications, and they reinforced it.” They followed the plan, and they reinforced it too. I think that's a job done with care.

That's it, baker! The text says, “When they were finished, they brought the rest of the money to the king and Jehoiada, and with it were made articles for the house of the LORD…” Jehoiada is the priest who, with the king, gave the money to the supervisors in verse 12. The leftovers went right back into the LORD's house.

Nope, friend, that money didn't get tucked away like the last cookie hidden behind the canisters. The workmen “…brought the rest of the money to the king and Jehoiada, and with it were made articles for the house of the LORD…” Jehoiada is the priest who worked with the king on this repair. The leftover money got turned into things for the house of the LORD.

You got it, baker. The text says, “Throughout the days of Jehoiada, burnt offerings were presented regularly in the house of the LORD.” The house was repaired, and the offerings were presented regularly. That's steady worship, friend, like an oven you can count on.

Rarely isn't the word, friend. The text says, “Throughout the days of Jehoiada, burnt offerings were presented regularly in the house of the LORD.” Regularly is the word the text gives. And the time it names is the days of Jehoiada.

Secretly isn't the word, baker. The text says, “Throughout the days of Jehoiada, burnt offerings were presented regularly in the house of the LORD.” Regularly is the word the text gives. The chest sat at the gate and the offerings kept coming.
That's a bigger number than the text gives, friend. It says, “When Jehoiada was old and full of years, he died at the age of 130.” It's a heavy verse, so we'll honor it and keep going.

That's right, baker. The text says Jehoiada “…was buried with the kings in the City of David, because he had done what was good in Israel for God and His temple.” Jehoiada is called the high priest in verse 6, and still he was buried with the kings. The text gives the reason right there in the verse.
